items.summary: An open-source experiment (MIT) from GitHub Next: several people and their coding agents collaborate in one channel, which runs on a teammate's Mac with channel traffic going host to host over the tailnet. Everyone running Ace on the same Tailscale network is automatically on the team, and API keys stay in the local keychain; the team directory can be deployed to your own Cloudflare or Fly.io account, or hosted by a single Mac. Agents run as you, with a shell and desktop apps, and a teammate's access to your agent starts off. Released November 9.
items.title: Ace: GitHub Next's multiplayer agent experiment — your Tailscale network is the team (released Nov 9, MIT)

items.summary: Tencent's open-source, self-hosted multi-agent R&D collaboration platform (MIT): hand Main Bot one requirement and it runs a six-stage SOP pipeline — clarify, design, implement, review, test, accept — in cloud sandboxes, with role handoffs, human approval gates and a full run record; scheduled tasks can sync GitHub Issues and fix routine tickets automatically. Five releases shipped November 9–13 and it hit GitHub trending on November 14. A Local edition installs the same workflow into the Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, CodeBuddy or Pi you already use with one npx command, no server needed.
items.title: LoopForge: Tencent's open-source self-hosted multi-agent R&D platform with SOP pipelines, sandboxes and human gates (released Nov 11, MIT)

items.summary: A self-hosted MCP server plus web dashboard (core MIT): Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Hermes and Ollama share one task inbox, and a dispatcher routes each task to a named brain — model × CLI × machine — verifies the result and falls back to the next brain on failure. Tasks live in files with no database, and 285 specialist personas are built in. Released November 14. Note: unrelated to Anthropic's same-named Claude Cowork.
items.title: Cowork: A self-hosted task inbox for many agents — one queue dispatches to Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and Hermes (released Nov 14, MIT)
